summary: Lassen National Forest lookout planned in 1932; a later site note says the building was removed and only foundation bolts remain.

facts.status_note: Building removed; only foundation bolts remain on the peak.

access.note: On Lassen National Forest land; a hiking app lists a trail named Ladder Butte Lookout. No structure remains to visit.

events.note: Site note dates a wooden building to 1932; the November 1932 letter still describes it as planned for spring
Telephone line proposed on Red River Lumber Company poles to link the planned lookout to the forest phone system
Surveyors visited and reported the wooden building in bad shape

evidence.supports: elevation 5,746 ft; located in Lassen National Forest
evidence.quote: Located in the Lassen National Forest, Elevation = 5746 ft.

evidence.supports: wooden building built 1932, still there 1948, bad shape
evidence.quote: A wooden building was built here in 1932 and it was there in 1948 when visited by surveyors, but was reported in bad shape.
Nothing remains at Ladder Butte but these foundation bolts.

evidence.quote: Photo July 16, 2012 looking west with Burney Mountain in view.

evidence.quote: It is our intention to build a lookout house on the peak before the beginning of the fire season next spring.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The November 1932 letter describes a lookout house planned for the spring; a later site note dates a wooden building to 1932. The sources disagree on the year.

sources.title: Best Hikes on Ladder Butte Lookout

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict: the November 9, 1932 letter plans construction for the next spring; the site note says built 1932. Removal date not found. The FFLA list also gives this gone site NHLR US 882, but that register page is not in cache. Access rests only on a hiking-app trail listing.
